mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 1.5% compresses equity discount rates by reducing risk-free rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days as investors shift capital from fixed income to equities.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly federal funds rate increase exceeding 0.25 percentage points signals imminent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as equity discount rates rise abruptly.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC < -0.03 over 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in federal funds rate and unemployment rate signal accommodative policy combined with labor market strength, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days through boosted earnings and reduced risk premiums.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p>0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE decline, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), labor market tightness sustains consumer spending and corporate margins, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as economic momentum persists.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%, or regime-specific Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in unemployment rate indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when UNRATE declines, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1250 thousand units signal weak consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as it foreshadows reduced economic activity and corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC < -0.03 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based consumer demand weakness, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days through reduced near-term economic growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p>0.05) when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105.0) signals robust manufacturing output that supports corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when INDPRO > 105.0, or regime-specific Rank IC < 0.03.
